scope: Bounded read-only adjudication of M1/M2 mission revision identity and storage; no implementation, phase audit, launches or test reruns.

decision.recommended_contract: Keep MissionSpec/RecordEnvelope.id equal to the original mission UUID across M1 and M2. Address mission revisions by (kind=mission, id, revision), and verify digest separately. M1Ref is (mission, original UUID, 1, original digest); M2Ref is (mission, same UUID, 2, independently computed digest).
decision.normative_certainty: Architecture does not expressly require every RecordEnvelope.id to remain stable across revisions, nor prescribe a storage primary key. It DOES require exact revision addressability, immutable history and a stable logical mission identity for cumulative focused budgeting. Stable MissionSpec.id is the recommended local contract, not a claim that the canon explicitly bans every alternative representation.
decision.distinct_revision_record_uuid_with_basis: NOT_ESTABLISHED_CANONICAL. A new UUID/revision=2 plus an arbitrary mission Ref in basis_refs proves neither unique same-mission lineage nor the meaning of future budget mission_id. basis_refs is a plural evidence/dependency field, not a specified predecessor/root relation. New UUID/revision=1 is expressly not a genuine M2. Distinct revision UUIDs could be architecture-compatible ONLY after specifying and enforcing an immutable stable logical mission/root identity, unique lineage/revision addressing and budget-key derivation; those are extra contracts absent from current sources. Do not adopt that alternative merely to retain the present PK.
decision.focused_budget_identity: Future (run_id, mission_id, FOCUS_BOOTSTRAP) uses the unchanged original mission UUID, not a revision storage UUID, revision number, new FocusEnvelope ID or fresh counter. An additive revision does not mint a new budget definition/deadline. The current finite FULL_ASSESSMENT path still has null bootstrap_budget_ref and zero/empty discovery; no focused bootstrap implementation is authorized.
decision.least_complex_scoped_storage: Retain managed_record as the existing immutable revision-1/FK ledger. Add one narrowly scoped immutable mission revision extension table for revision=2, anchored to its original mission row and composite-addressed by (mission_id, revision). This avoids changing any existing managed_run/task/inbox FK target or rebuilding historical envelopes. It is a proposed additional table requiring explicit parent scope authorization, not an already implemented or proven-minimum DDL design.
decision.why_this_over_global_surrogate_rekey: All existing FK-targeted kinds remain revision1 and their original IDs remain exact row identities. Only mission requires the new revision. A mission-only extension localizes new SQL addressing while leaving historical managed_record PK, envelope.id=id and revision=1 constraints intact. A global surrogate/composite migration is coherent but changes a much larger established storage contract without a current consumer requiring generalized revisions.

canonical_sources.supports: Historical ingest, current qualification and new admission are distinct; preserve A/M1 after additive M2; invalid state requires revalidation/ineligibility; exact ResultQualification refs, no automatic functional PASS.
Obligation/execution identities are semantic and structured; revision/UUID churn is not a reason to repeat work or reset limits.
Cumulative focused bootstrap definition is keyed by run_id/mission_id and preserved across additive revisions/re-entry/restart; FULL_ASSESSMENT has no focused budget.
Authority keys/FKs are constrained columns; scoped ownership requires composite FKs or validation, not guessed-ID joins.
Strict Ref includes kind/id/revision/digest; exact canonical digest includes backend-owned ID and revision; every revision immutable; physical storage not prescribed.

Mission has basis_refs but no specified predecessor or logical-root field. Mission/focus append-only under immutable request; consumers cite consumed revision; material objective/mode change requires Stop/new run.

observed_blockers.finding: managed_record.id PK plus envelope.id=id and revision=1 prevent same-ID revision2; immutable trigger prevents rewriting M1.
Existing run/manifest/binding/final/brief/result/check/inbox FKs target managed_record(id); preserve those exact meanings.
record() rejects every revision other than integer1 before storage/readback/graph verification.
put/by_id/get/owned/graph assume one managed_record row per envelope UUID; get already compares complete canonical Ref after lookup.
Graph uniqueness/lookup is ID-only, including historical mission selection; cannot safely admit M1+M2 with stable ID.
Outcome reconstruction uses an ID-only map and must resolve the mission from the historical header's exact Ref; last-row-wins would silently select M2.
Builder requires exactly one retained mission. Keep revised-context new-work preparation refused; do not replace this with latest mission or resurrect an existing assignment.

minimal_coherent_prerequisite_slice.observable_acceptance: An owned mission M1 and a genuine backend-authored M2 with the same mission UUID/revision2 coexist durably; exact reads and retained M1 graph/result/check reconstruction work without historical byte changes; nonmission revisions remain exactly1; revised-context prepare remains refused and grants no new work.
ddl_contract: Keep managed_record PK and all existing external FKs and its existing envelope/revision1/immutability checks unchanged. Add a UNIQUE(id,owner_id,run_id) root key if using the recommended composite ownership FK; this is additive DDL, not record mutation.

Add managed_mission_revision with mission_id uuid, owner_id uuid, run_id uuid, revision bigint, envelope jsonb; all NOT NULL; PRIMARY KEY(mission_id,revision); FOREIGN KEY(mission_id,owner_id,run_id) REFERENCES managed_record(id,owner_id,run_id). The current slice accepts revision=2 ONLY; no generalized arbitrary positive revisions.

Strict SQL constraints require object envelope, kind=mission, UUID envelope.id=mission_id, numeric integer envelope.revision=revision, numeric integer schema_version=1. Missing/null/string/boolean/fractional fields must fail, including CHECK-NULL loopholes. Keep canonical envelope fields only in authored validation and digest resealing/readback.

Validate the immutable root is exactly kind mission/revision1 under the same owner/run. A root-kind insertion guard must be enforced and exactly attested, not merely assumed from the FK, because managed_record contains multiple kinds. Verify the exact M1Ref occurs once as the mission predecessor in M2 basis_refs; forbid a second mission basis for this finite transition, self-basis and foreign/unavailable/wrong-digest basis. This is a new narrow lineage interpretation to record explicitly, not an existing meaning of generic basis_refs.

Block UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on the extension table, preserving M1 and M2. Do not add mutable latest-mission pointer, ledger, scheduler, admission table or new runtime owner. Store M1 only in managed_record and M2 only in the extension, preventing two physical copies of a revision.

Do not hash JSONB serialization. Use the existing CanonicalJSON envelope rule; compute M2 digest from same mission UUID, integer2 and authored payload, then independently validate it on read. PostgreSQL JSONB semantic storage is not proof of original wire-byte retention.
source_contract: Use a specialized backend mission-revision constructor/validator; leave candidate_store.envelope's generic UUID/revision1 defaults and catalog_record storage unchanged. Validate exact schema, finite same-request lineage and allowed additive content before writes. Storage success by itself is not a compatibility or freshness proof.

Allow managed_contract.record revision2 only for a strictly validated mission. Every other kind, including focus, task-result, method-check, contract-input-command, qualification and catalog-side records, remains exactly integer1 in this slice. Boolean/string revisions never coerce.

managed_store.get/owned resolve mission by id+revision then compare full Ref including digest and ownership; by_id remains the explicit legacy revision1/FK-row lookup and never means latest. graph merges base and extension deterministically by kind/id/revision, without dropping M1 or M2.

Graph uniqueness is on (kind,id,revision), and same (kind,id,revision) with different digest/payload is conflict. Resolve every mission from exact consumed Ref, especially historic criterion outcome reconstruction; an ID-only dictionary containing multiple mission revisions is forbidden. Keep nonmission legacy lookups explicitly revision1 rather than overwriting.

readback must use the unified graph reader; its current direct SELECT managed_record otherwise hides M2. Do not rewrite managed-run/context/focus/cursor/brief/header/TaskResult/MethodCheck to point at M2; those remain the original consumed M1 refs.

Preparation for new work on a revised mission/context explicitly refuses before assignment persistence or native effects. Existing single-mission builder fail-closed behavior remains; idempotent retrieval of an already admitted M1 receipt is historical readback, not permission to dispatch it again.

No ResultQualification semantics, semantic dedup engine, replan, coverage denominator, auth freshness or focused ledger implementation in this prerequisite. Qualification work follows separately, on finite retained current records and proof of compatibility.

necessary_source_consumers.action: Add exact extension table columns/constraints and additive root key; retain base revision1 checks.

Exact attestation must include new immutability and root-insert guard definitions/types/enabled state, not only columns/constraint names. Existing trigger attestor expects exactly one immutable trigger per listed table and cannot blindly absorb a second guard.
Single exact new head; old head stays incompatible, no readiness auto-migration.
Mission-only revision2 validator and revised-context new-admission refusal; preserve generic/nonmission revision1.
Narrow extension write, composite mission resolution, graph union, exact command replay/readback; reuse managed-owner transaction lock.
Ref-key graph validation/historical mission resolution; unified readback; explicitly prevent M2 new-work prepare. The retained-map/dedup path must not collapse revisions if reachable.
Select historical mission by exact header Ref for outcomes; never current/latest mission. Preserve original checks/outcomes.
Owning command/transaction seam for later additive mission write; existing context's M1 refs remain exact. No new admission authority in prerequisite.
ID-only new-composition maps remain safe ONLY behind explicit revised-graph refusal. Do not widen native/composer acceptance to make M2 admission work.
Leave generic catalog envelope/PK/ref behavior unchanged; do not globally generalize catalog storage.

source_identity_cutover.risk: managed_contract.py and criterion_checks.py are checker fingerprint closure members. Editing them changes current checker identity even if the method algorithm is unchanged; M1 MethodCheck readback would otherwise fail against the new descriptor.
source_identity_cutover.required: Capture the exact pre-edit checker descriptor/composer pair from the current bytes and preserve that exact identity as receive-only compatibility, with independent unchanged historical payload reconstruction/equality. Also capture the pre-edit criterion_checks.py SHA: criterion-outcome-rule.code_digest hashes that whole file (criterion_checks.py:46-58), and receive-only validation recognizes only exact HISTORICAL_RULES entries and supported check states (criterion_checks.py:20-25,189-193,247-249). A ref-key lookup edit changes that rule identity; preserve the original exact digest and actually supported COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE/UNKNOWN states only after proving unchanged historical outcome reconstruction. Do not rewrite old checker/rule records or digests, force current descriptors to old bytes, or admit historical pins for new preparation. Fresh fixtures must use freshly qualified current bytes. Native/composer source need not change for this storage slice.

UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on either historical or extension ledger refuses; mutate/remove/disable trigger or change default/PK/FK/check validation/enforcement and exact schema readiness refuses.
